Lavender EO (French, L. angustifolia).source: GC-MS of commercial market samples: linalyl acetate 37.8, linalool 33.1, eucalyptol 4.9, camphor 4.1; minor terpenes from the same literature range.
Lavender EO (French, L. angustifolia).note: The default for an unqualified 'lavender oil' in a perfumery formula.

Lavender EO (Spanish, var. pyrenaica).source: linalool 38.0, borneol 19.7, camphor 8.1, cineole ~3, linalyl acetate ~1.1

Lavender EO (South African).note: Barely a lavender by odour; kept as the negative control, since a method that calls this one lavender is not discriminating.

Petitgrain EO (bigarade).source: Reference ranges for petitgrain bigarade: linalyl acetate 51-71, linalool 12-24, terpineol 2-5, geraniol 1-2, geranyl acetate 1-3, nerol <1. Midpoints used.
Petitgrain EO (bigarade).note: In the perfumer's inventory. An Egyptian GC/MS study puts linalool far higher, 30-34%, against linalyl acetate above 25 -- the sources disagree about which ester-to-alcohol ratio is typical, and this build takes the ester-heavy one.

Cedarwood EO (Virginia).source: Supplier GC ranges for Virginia type: alpha-cedrene plus funebrene 20-35, thujopsene 10-35, cedrol 16-25, beta-cedrene plus caryophyllene 4-8, alpha-cuparene 1.5-7, widdrol 2-5. Midpoints used; a single-batch GC-MS citing Lawrence 1980 agrees closely at cedrol 26.1, alpha-cedrene 24.6, thujopsene 15.1.
Cedarwood EO (Virginia).note: In the perfumer's inventory. The weakest build here: thujopsene is a fifth of the oil and is not in the library, so the weights renormalise over cedrene and cedrol and the result is a cleaner, less dry wood than the real oil.

Bergamot EO (Turkish).source: Peer-reviewed analysis of Turkish bergamot oil, 2000: linalyl acetate 38.7, limonene 23.7, linalool 14.7, gamma-terpinene 4.7, beta-pinene 3.0, myrcene 2.0.
Bergamot EO (Turkish).note: Other origins range linalyl acetate 19-41%, limonene 24-44%, linalool 7-26%, so this is one profile out of a wide family.

Geranium EO (Bourbon, Madagascar).source: Supplier specification by ISO 4731: citronellol 23.2, geraniol 15.5, isomenthone 8.2, linalool 5.9, cis-rose oxide 1.1, trans-rose oxide 0.4.

Peppermint EO (Michigan).source: Kubeczka 1993 via TGSC: menthol 38.01, menthone 23.14, menthyl acetate 3.69, menthofuran 2.48, limonene 2.44, beta-pinene 1.65, gamma-terpinene 0.68.

Clove Bud EO (steam distilled).source: Turkish steam-distilled analysis: eugenol 87.00, eugenyl acetate 8.01, beta-caryophyllene 3.56.
Clove Bud EO (steam distilled).note: Near enough a single molecule that predicting 'clove' from it is close to trivial; included for formula coverage rather than as a test.

Orange EO (sweet, Florida).source: Commercial GC-MS profile, Myers & Lee: limonene ~91, myrcene ~1.5, citral ~0.06, beta-pinene ~0.01, gamma-terpinene ~0.01. Other sweet orange profiles put limonene at 95-98.
Orange EO (sweet, Florida).note: Effectively limonene. An oil this dominated by one constituent is barely a mixture, so the build is close to a rename of D-Limonene and should not be read as the model understanding orange oil.

Lime EO (Persian, expressed).source: Persian lime profile: limonene ~52, gamma-terpinene ~14, beta-pinene ~12, citral up to 2.8, myrcene ~1.4. Across lime entries limonene runs 49-56 and gamma-terpinene 12-14.
Lime EO (Persian, expressed).note: The one citrus here that is a real mixture rather than limonene with traces. Expressed, not distilled: distilled lime rearranges under acid into p-cymene and terpinen-4-ol and smells quite different, and neither is in the library.

Tangerine EO.source: GC-MS of tangerine oil: limonene ~95 (range 84-97 across dilutions), gamma-terpinene and beta-pinene in traces only.
Tangerine EO.note: Included on request, and it should be expected to fail to separate from orange. What makes a tangerine smell like a tangerine rather than an orange is methyl N-methylanthranilate plus thymol, and no source gave a usable figure for the first; the library holds Methyl Anthranilate, which is a different molecule, so substituting it would be a fabrication rather than an approximation. What is built here is therefore limonene with traces, like the orange.

Cinnamon Bark EO (commercial).source: GC-MS of commercial oil: cinnamal 63.59, eugenol 8.32, cinnamyl acetate 7.48, caryophyllene 6.88, linalool 6.31, eucalyptol 2.57.
